lessons: Keep the ProviderRuntime design, the single Timers lifetime, the shared-payload caller migration, and the Registry-built-once-in-_locked Refusal fix. Review accepted all of them. Change only what the findings below name.

Single-candidate cooldown must truly park. Right now ProviderRuntime.resolve raises a bare RoutingError, which Driver turns into infra_error, and runner.py:359 then consumes INFRA_CAP on every dispatch during the cooldown. That can reject the ticket before timer_fired.

Fix the park: raise a classified ProviderError (failure_class quota_exhausted, with a paved_road naming the cooldown deadline). Outcome routing should treat it as a hold, not an INFRA_CAP draw. Or skip dispatch until the cooldown Timer fires. Do not reuse RoutingError, which means a config refusal.

Fail over within the same call. After cool_down(provider) in CliClient.call, retry the next eligible configured candidate in order. Raise only when no candidate is eligible, so a quota hit does not waste an attempt or INFRA_CAP while another candidate is free.

Resolve once per call. WatchdogLLM (watchdog.py:228) and the inner CliClient each call resolve, so a cooldown firing between the two can make the watchdog record the wrong served identity and cost basis. Pass the chosen Resolved down, or read identity from the client's result.

Add runner-level tests to tests/test_provider_cooldown_failover.py. A single-candidate quota hit consumes no INFRA_CAP while the cooldown is live and becomes dispatchable after timer_fired. The first quota-hit request is served by the later candidate.
reason: Review found fixable wiring gaps (a non-parking single-candidate cooldown, failover only on the next call, a double resolve) inside the existing fence, and it gave clear paved roads.
